title: Entick v Carrington (1765)
summary: General warrants to search and seize papers were unlawful; executive power is limited by law.
principle: Rule of law constraints on executive search and seizure.

title: Donoghue v Stevenson (1932)
summary: Established the modern law of negligence and the 'neighbour principle' in the House of Lords.
principle: Duty of care in tort shaping private-law obligations.

title: Ridge v Baldwin (1964)
summary: Public office-holders are entitled to natural justice before dismissal in many contexts.
principle: Procedural fairness in public employment decisions.

title: R (Factortame Ltd) v Secretary of State for Transport (No 2) (1991)
summary: EU law could disapply inconsistent UK statutes and courts could grant interim relief—central to supremacy debates.
principle: Interaction of EU and domestic law before Brexit-era changes.

title: A v Secretary of State for the Home Department (Belmarsh, 2004)
summary: House of Lords reviewed indefinite detention of non-UK nationals under anti-terror legislation.
principle: Liberty, proportionality, and detention without trial in security contexts.

title: R v Secretary of State for the Home Department, ex parte Simms (1999)
summary: Common law may fill gaps where legislation is silent; prisoners' access to media for innocence claims discussed.

title: R v Shayler (2002)
summary: Official Secrets Act restrictions assessed for compatibility with ECHR free-expression rights.
principle: National security secrecy versus freedom of expression.
